title: Floquet spin-group framework and its application to light-tailored spin splitting in collinear magnets
authors: Tongshuai Zhu, Zixuan Li, Huaiqiang Wang, Su-Huai Wei, Jiawei Ruan
abstract: Altermagnets combine momentum-dependent spin splitting with vanishing net magnetization, opening new opportunities for spintronics. Recent studies have shown that periodic driving by linearly or circularly polarized light, as well as by multicolor light fields, can control spin splitting in altermagnets and conventional antiferromagnets, and can even generate spin splitting patterns absent in equilibrium. Despite this progress, a unified principle connecting the dynamical symmetry of light to the symmetry of spin-split bands remains lacking, limiting the systematic design of light-induced spin structures. Here, by combining the spin group of crystals with the dynamical group of light, we establish a unified Floquet spin group framework for the study of periodically driven collinear magnets with negligible spin-orbit coupling. This framework systematically determines the allowed parity, momentum dependence, and nodal structure of spin splitting under different driving protocols. Guided by this symmetry classification, we show that odd-parity, even-parity, and mixed-parity spin splittings can be switched within the same material by tailoring the driving field. We further uncover higher-order $h$-wave and $k$-wave spin splittings in three-dimensional systems. Our work establishes a unified symmetry framework for light-controlled spin splitting and provides general principles for engineering nonequilibrium spin-band structures in altermagnets and related magnetic materials.
summary: This paper introduces a novel Floquet spin-group framework that unifies the study of light-induced spin splitting in collinear magnets. By combining crystal symmetry with the dynamical symmetry of polarized light, the authors provide systematic rules for engineering specific types of electronic band structures. This allows researchers to precisely control magnetic properties by tailoring external optical driving fields.
main_problem: The primary goal is establishing a unified symmetry principle connecting the dynamical symmetry of incident light to the resulting spin-split electronic band structures in magnetic materials.
main_result: The authors developed a Floquet spin-group framework that systematically classifies allowed parity and momentum dependence for light-induced spin splittings, enabling the switching between different splitting types (odd, even, mixed) using tailored driving fields.
method: The methodology combines crystal spin point group theory with the dynamical symmetry group of light to define a governing Floquet spin group ($\mathcal{G}_D$). This framework is applied via time-dependent Hamiltonian analysis and quasienergy constraints.
model_or_system: The study focuses on collinear magnets, particularly altermagnets (AM) and antiferromagnets (AFM), modeled with negligible spin-orbit coupling. The system dynamics are governed by a Floquet Hamiltonian derived from periodic driving by light fields (CPL or BLPL).
key_observables: Spin-resolved quasienergy bands, the parity of spin splitting (odd/even/mixed), and higher-order wave splittings ($h$-wave, $k$-wave).
important_parameters: The driving field parameters, such as polarization type (CPL vs. BLPL) and relative phases ($\alpha$), act as crucial tuning knobs.
main_assumptions: The framework is initially developed for collinear magnets with negligible spin-orbit coupling, although it claims general applicability.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the generators defining the dynamical light group ($	ilde{G}_L$) and provide schematic classification tables showing how different light symmetries dictate the resulting parity of spin splittings in AMs.
paper_structure: The paper introduces the problem by noting the lack of a unified symmetry principle. It then develops the Floquet spin-group framework, applies it to classify various splitting types (2D and 3D), and concludes with specific examples demonstrating how light polarization controls these symmetries.
why_interesting: This work provides a powerful theoretical tool—a symmetry classification scheme—to predict and engineer electronic properties in magnetic materials using external electromagnetic fields, which is highly relevant to quantum optics and open quantum systems research.

(a) The symmetries of a collinear compensated magnet can be described by spin groups, whereas the symmetries of different light can be characterized by dynamical groups. For circular polarized light (CPL) with vector potential A0(cos ωt, sin ωt, 0), the generators of the dynamical group are [E||Cn]·τn, [T ||mx]·τ2, [E||P]·τ2, and for bilinear polarized light (BLPL) with vector potential A0(sin ωt, sin 2ωt, 0), the generators are [E||mx] · τ2, [T ||E] · τE (see main text for the details). Spintronics.note: The paper directly addresses the interaction between optical driving fields (light) and magnetic/spin structures (collinear magnets), which is central to quantum-optics concepts applied to spintronic materials.
